title: Story Time
intro: Past simple, past continuous or past perfect? Pick the form that tells the story right.

B2.q: The sheriff ___ his coffee when the stagecoach rolled into town.
B2.why: A longer action in progress (was drinking) is interrupted by a shorter one (rolled).

B2.q: By the time the posse reached the canyon, the outlaws ___ .
B2.why: “By the time” points back to something that happened earlier: past perfect.

B2.q: When Fleming came back from holiday, he found that, during his absence, mould ___ all over one of his dishes.
B2.why: The mould grew while he was away, before he found it: past perfect for the earlier event.

B2.q: While John Snow ___ the map of cholera deaths, he saw that they clustered around one water pump.
B2.why: “While” + past continuous sets the background action.

B2.q: The cowboy ___ his horse, rode out of town and never came back.
B2.why: A chain of finished actions told in order: past simple for each one.

B2.q: When the ranchers woke up, the plain was white: it ___ during the night.
B2.why: The snow fell before they woke up, so it goes one step further back: past perfect.

B2.q: In 1796 Edward Jenner ___ a boy with material from a milkmaid's cowpox sores.
B2.why: A single finished event at a stated past date: past simple. The present perfect cannot go with “in 1796”.

B2.q: The doctors ___ for hours when the patient finally opened his eyes.
B2.why: Duration up to a moment in the past (“for hours … when”): past perfect continuous.

B2.q: As the train ___ the desert, two masked men jumped onto the roof.
B2.why: The train was in the middle of crossing when the men jumped: past continuous for the background.
“Before 1928” looks back from a point in the past: past perfect.

B2.q: The marshal was exhausted because he ___ for three days without sleep.
B2.why: A long activity that explains a past result (exhausted): past perfect continuous.

B2.q: In 1885 Jaume Ferran, a doctor working in Valencia, ___ the first cholera vaccine to be used on people.
B2.why: A finished achievement at a stated past date: past simple.

B2.q: She couldn't pay for her drink because she ___ her purse at the hotel.
B2.why: Leaving the purse happened before the moment she tried to pay: past perfect, not the present perfect.

B2.q: The town was almost empty: most of the miners ___ to the next gold field a month earlier.
B2.why: “A month earlier”, seen from a past moment, needs the past perfect.

B1.q: I ___ dinner when the phone rang.
B1.why: An action in progress (was cooking) interrupted by a short one (rang).

B1.q: Yesterday we ___ to the market and bought some oranges.
B1.why: Finished actions in order, yesterday: past simple.

B1.q: When I arrived at the party, Ana ___ home.
B1.why: Ana left before I arrived: past perfect for the earlier action.

B1.q: It ___ when we came out of the cinema, so we took a taxi.
B1.why: The rain was the background at that moment: past continuous.

B1.q: While the cowboys ___ dinner by the fire, a coyote howled.
B1.why: “While” + past continuous for the longer background action.

B1.q: What ___ you doing at eight o'clock last night?
B1.why: A question about an action in progress at a past time: was/were + -ing.

B1.q: When I met him again last year, I didn't recognise him because he ___ a big beard.
B1.why: The beard grew before that meeting, and the meeting is already in the past: past perfect, had grown.

B1.q: She ___ her leg while she was skiing.
B1.why: The short, sudden event that interrupts the longer one: past simple.

B1.q: We ___ the film before, so we chose a different one.
B1.why: Seeing the film happened before choosing: past perfect.

B1.q: The sun ___ as we walked along the beach in Valencia.
B1.why: Background description during the walk: past continuous.
A single finished event at a stated date: past simple.

B1.q: The nurse ___ the patient some water and then went home.
B1.why: Two finished actions in order: past simple, then past simple.
